segments.title: Chương 69: Về nhà ăn Tết
segments.content:
Returning to Rongcheng, reporter Chen Feng wrote the article the very next day.

But he wasn't in a hurry to submit it for publication.

Good news like this should definitely avoid the Spring Festival.

During the New Year, there were too many lively and joyous events, and any news would get less attention.

He planned to publish it after the fifteenth day of the first lunar month!

And continue to revise the draft in the meantime.

Meanwhile, the day after Chen Guiliang returned to Longdu, he used his granduncle's landline to call Bian Guanyue.

"You finally called. I couldn't get through to your PHS phone," Bian Guanyue said excitedly.

Chen Guiliang asked, "Has anyone contacted you?"

"Both Fudan and Beijing Normal University called, and Fudan even thought I was..." Bian Guanyue swallowed her words. She was too embarrassed to mention that part. "Wait a minute, I'll go get a notebook and read their preferential terms to you."

Chen Guiliang listened carefully.

After reading them, Bian Guanyue said again, "Chen Guiliang, you're amazing!"

Chen Guiliang chuckled, "I'm amazing in many ways."

Bian Guanyue also laughed, "Are you choosing Fudan or Beijing Normal?"

Chen Guiliang said, "Let's wait a bit longer. After the New Year holiday, other universities might call. Whatever they say, don't agree to anything. Just help me take notes."

"Okay, I understand."

As she spoke, Bian Guanyue couldn't help but praise, "Those two poems you wrote are brilliant!"

"Did you see them online or in the newspaper?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Bian Guanyue said, "Online. You've become famous on many forums. I even saw someone reposting it on Mop today."

Chen Guiliang heard a cat meowing over the phone. "Is the kitten okay?"

"She's very well-behaved and very clingy. Whenever I stop, she wants to climb on me. I even gave her a name, Huajuan," Bian Guanyue said with a giggle.

Chen Guiliang said, "The one at my home is called Xiongmao'er."

Bian Guanyue said, "Very descriptive."

The "-er" suffix in the Sichuan dialect was just as common as in the north, and "Xiongmao'er" was the standard way to say it.

After some idle chat, Chen Guiliang hung up and called Tao Xue.

"Are you home?"

"Yes. Haha, I saw the poem you wrote."

"What about your brother?"

"He's here too."

"Give me the address, I'll be right over."

Chen Guiliang dragged his suitcase, bid farewell to his granduncle and grandaunt, and then took a taxi to the Tao family's home.

Two adjacent commodity apartments. Tao Xue lived in one with her parents, and Tao Chenggang lived in the other by himself.

On the phone, Chen Guiliang heard what sounded like guests at Tao Xue's home, so he chose to ring Tao Chenggang's doorbell.

"Have a seat, no need to change your shoes," Tao Chenggang said, opening the door to welcome him.

Seeing him in a suit and tie, Chen Guiliang joked, "Brother Gang, are you going on a blind date?"

"You actually guessed right. Sigh!" Tao Chenggang sighed.

It was the child of a leader from his parents' factory, a bachelor's degree graduate working in a foreign company. Since she was back home for the New Year, they insisted Tao Chenggang meet her.

Chen Guiliang said, "My granduncle told me about the subsequent profit-sharing for the private server. Brother Gang has been running around to nearby cities and counties, negotiating with internet cafes, and I haven't been much help. So, I won't take any more profit shares after the New Year."

In two months, Chen Guiliang could probably get about 140,000 yuan.

That was enough. There was no need to be greedy.

Besides, Abyss Legend was already on a decline, with its revenue gradually decreasing in the second month. This was because more and more similar Legend private servers were emerging, and the dungeon gameplay was no longer fresh.

It was always a one-shot deal, and during the special crackdown, low-cost promotion was impossible.

Tao Chenggang wasn't particularly happy to hear this. "You're not going to participate in developing our own game either?"

"I can help with some ideas," Chen Guiliang said.

Tao Chenggang thought for a moment. "How about this? I'll invest all your future profit shares from the private server into game development, and convert it into company shares based on the specific amount."

Chen Guiliang neither refused nor immediately agreed. "Didn't I already sell you the free-to-play game concept and gameplay?"

"I've always believed that business is about people," Tao Chenggang said. "I think we can have better development by working with you."

Chen Guiliang said, "If we start a company, I'll be unhappy if I hold too few shares. But if I take too many, Brother Gang, you definitely won't be happy either. I'll help you as much as I can, and we can decide based on the specific situation after the company grows. At that time, I can continue to hold the shares. If you're willing to buy them, I can also sell them to you."

The investment in Tao Chenggang's project was too large, and it was highly likely to fail due to a lack of funds. Chen Guiliang didn't want to get involved.

He had a more stable and profitable game project. He might even make money before Tao Chenggang and then turn around to invest in Tao Chenggang's half-finished game.

Tao Chenggang asked, "Are you planning to start your own company?"

Chen Guiliang didn't hide it. "Also in gaming. But the game I want to make is different from Brother Gang's free-to-play game, so we won't be in direct competition."

After some thought, Chen Guiliang added, "Since Brother Gang is willing to give me shares, I'll return the favor and write a game design document for you during the New Year. It will only include the overall concept, system design, and plot design. I won't bother with the more detailed and professional stuff."

"Good, it's a deal then." This was exactly what Tao Chenggang wanted.

The special crackdown by the five ministries and commissions would last for three months. Many tech experts in the private server business were lying low during this time.

Tao Chenggang took the opportunity to reel in a batch of technical talents. Some of these talents were wealthy themselves and could even be persuaded to invest as minority shareholders.

But no one had ever developed their own game before. Fearing that more business secrets would be leaked, Tao Chenggang dared not discuss the details with them for the time being. He tried to write a game design document himself, but he wasn't satisfied with either of the two drafts he produced, so he set his sights on Chen Guiliang.

Chen Guiliang didn't mind. He just considered it making a friend. After all, he just had to write a little during the Spring Festival and wouldn't need to put in any other effort.

Just then, Tao Xue came running over.

"Why didn't you come to my place?" Tao Xue complained.

Chen Guiliang smiled and took out three signed books. "I didn't want to disturb your parents. These are the autographs I got for you."

Tao Xue opened the title page and saw that each book's signature included her name and a well-wishing message. Instantly, all her unhappiness vanished.

"I'll give you credit for being thoughtful." Tao Xue sat down beside Chen Guiliang, beaming.

It was only then that Tao Chenggang realized something was off. His sister seemed to...

They seemed to be a good match!

Tao Chenggang glanced at his watch, stood up, and said, "I have to go to my blind date. You two take your time chatting. Remember to close the door when you leave."

The guy quickly slipped away, creating an opportunity for his sister to be alone with Chen Guiliang.

Chen Guiliang also wanted to leave, but Tao Xue held him back to talk. "Is the real Su Tong as handsome as he is in pictures?"

"He's a handsome middle-aged man, looks quite energetic," Chen Guiliang said.

"What about Yu Hua?"

"He's alright too."

"Did you talk about literature with them?"

"No, we were too busy shooting the breeze."

"..."

After about twenty minutes of idle chat, Chen Guiliang ignored Tao Xue's invitation to stay for a meal, insisting he had something urgent to attend to at home.

He took a bus to the old district, bought some cured meats for the New Year, and then, right on the heels of the bamboo pole scam, took a taxi back to the village. These taxi drivers were real sharks around the Spring Festival!

Back in the village, it felt like being cut off from the world again.

The villagers knew nothing about the New Concept Competition, let alone that Chen Guiliang had become a celebrity.

Even the already famous Guo Xiaosi, who hailed from this very city, was unknown to these villagers. On the other hand, Zhao Yanzi was a household name; men and women, old and young, all loved to watch "My Fair Princess."

"Niangniang, I'm back." Arriving home, Chen Guiliang found his grandmother spring cleaning.

Her physical strength was limited, so she couldn't do much at once. It had taken her several days of busy work.

The cobwebs in the corners and on the ceiling had been cleared away by Grandma.

The tables, stools, cabinets, and bed frames had all been wiped clean.

Even the chicken and duck coops had been thoroughly cleaned.

Grandma put down her broom. "Have you had lunch?"

"I've eaten." Chen Guiliang had grabbed a few buns while buying the cured meats.

Grandma didn't ask if he had won an award, only saying, "You must be tired from the long train ride. Go take a nap."

"I came back last night and stayed at my granduncle's place," Chen Guiliang asked, "Niangniang, has Xiongmao'er been good?"

Grandma said sarcastically, "Very good!"

Chen Guiliang laughed heartily. He had intentionally bought a mischievous black-and-white cat because his grandmother was too lonely at home by herself.

"Xiongmao'er. Meow!"

Chen Guiliang had also bought a jin of small fish. He casually tossed them into the courtyard.

Smelling the fish, Xiongmao'er shot out from somewhere.

Chen Guiliang took the New Year goods and the fish to the kitchen. Seeing that the water vat was only a quarter full, he picked up the carrying pole and buckets to fetch water.

After finishing the fish, Xiongmao'er familiarly followed Chen Guiliang.

The doorstep was too high for it to jump over at once. It struggled to climb like it was scaling a mountain, and after much effort, it tumbled over the threshold with a plop.

"Meow!"

Chen Guiliang was already far away with the buckets. Xiongmao'er scrambled up and chased after him, meowing.

When it reached a patch of grass, it decisively abandoned Chen Guiliang and dived into the dense wild grass to frolic.

When Chen Guiliang brought a bucket of water back, he found Xiongmao'er squatting on the path waiting for him. A mouse lay beside its paws, and it was meowing incessantly as if to claim credit.

"No way, you're so young. You can already catch mice?" Chen Guiliang found it amusing.

The mouse was also very small and had been tormented into playing dead.

Xiongmao'er pawed at it a few times. Finding the little mouse motionless, it lost interest and lay down to sleep beside it.

The little mouse took the chance to escape. It had barely moved ten centimeters when Xiongmao'er's paw came down on it.

By the time Chen Guiliang returned with the third bucket of water, the little mouse had been tortured to death.

Chen Guiliang went to the kitchen, got a pair of fire tongs, and clamped the mouse's body to throw it into the latrine pit.

"Meow meow~~~"

Xiongmao'er kept crying out, seemingly very displeased.

"Oh, Big Brother Chen, Second Sister Yao are back for the New Year!"

A neighbor's voice came from behind the house.

Chen Guiliang stopped fetching water and walked to the edge of the courtyard to wait. Soon, he saw his parents walking over, carrying large and small bags.

"Liangliang, you've grown so tall!" Yao Lan exclaimed with delight.

The last time she left home, her son was still a few months shy of ten. Now, he was a handsome young man.

Leaning on a long-handled broom, Grandma stood silently under the eaves, smiling as she watched the three of them.

After nearly eight years, the family was finally reunited.
